text:
Jeremy Swayman spent most of the first month looking like the goalie who carried Boston last season, and the last week looking human. The high point came Nov. 8: 40 saves in a 4-1 win over Florida that gave the Bruins four straight wins, as NHL.com reported. Then Montreal chased him after 28 minutes on Nov. 12, and Minnesota scored five on him two nights later.

Zoom out and he's still well above water: 6.0 goals saved above expected (goals stopped beyond what the shots were worth), 79th percentile among goalies, with a 9-5-1 record and a .905 save percentage. Where it comes from is the interesting part. On medium-danger shots he's at .916 against a league .863, worth about 7.5 goals on its own. On the true high-danger looks he's been slightly below what those shots usually allow.

That's a pattern to watch more than a worry. Last season he saved 26.5 goals above expected in 55 games, and two rough nights don't erase that. The Anchorage native won the Jennings Trophy in 2022-23 and went to the Olympics with the U.S. in February. Boston's season still runs through him.
